superseded.reason: This is the artifact as first admitted. Two review rounds then found the keyTangent read-back useless (it set Maya's default), the selection unmeasured, the scene guard blind to unsaved untitled scenes, and the shipped test's own assertion no stronger than the driver's. The final artifact records the run that exercised the fixed driver and test. Kept unchanged apart from this block, per docs/evidence/README.md.

meta.purpose: Turn #229's six 'static check passed but real Maya never ran' call forms into measured pass/fail rows on a real Maya 2024 session.
meta.verdict: 6/6 call forms pass on Maya 2024; the shipped pytest function tests/test_mayapy_smoke.py::test_callform_stub_disagreement_forms passes when called with the real maya.cmds; a probe that raises after creating nodes leaves no node behind; the scene returns to its starting node count and playback range.
meta.claim_boundary: Proves these six call forms work on Maya 2024 on Windows (GUI batch=False session). It does NOT prove Maya 2025/2026, and does not prove the mayapy/standalone lane — mayapy cannot import maya.standalone on this box (DLL initialisation failure), so batch-mode behaviour such as cmds.about(batch=True) stays unverified here. Values recorded are one run per form; the forms are asserted by the shipped test, not by this artifact alone.

notes.kWorld_type: Maya's om2.MSpace.kWorld is a plain int; getPoint accepts it. So the stub's parameter type (MSpace) is the wrong half, not the constant: the constant is int, exactly as the stub declares.
notes.rename_clash: Maya returns GEO_cf253_renamed1 for the second node wanting that name and keeps the first node alive, so the return value must be used, not the requested name.
notes.scene_state: Node count 51 before and after; playback 1.0-120.0 before and after; no GEO_cf253*/GEO_stub* node left. The instance was a fresh throwaway GUI and was quit by the wrapper, so no user scene was involved at any point.
